author: KanekoaTheGreat
text:
🚨 BREAKING: I found four documented cases involving .30-06 rounds whose bullets failed to exit, including Charlie Kirk’s case.

A fifth case involved a 7.62×54R round, a ballistically similar cartridge, whose bullet also failed to exit.

On March 20, 2008, Berry Hall shot his neighbor, Lisa Tackett, with a .30-06 from an upstairs bedroom window.

The bullet entered her left breast, traveled through her organs and torso, lodged in her right chest wall without exiting, and was removed during autopsy.

The court record does not indicate that it struck bone, unlike the soft-point bullet that killed Charlie and reportedly “obliterated” his C2–C7 vertebrae before lodging in his body.

The case is documented in the Kentucky Supreme Court’s 2015 and 2022 opinions in Hall v. Commonwealth.

@BretWeinstein, @RealCandaceO, @IanCarrollShow, @jimmy_dore and other Tyler Robinson defenders claim Charlie’s wound was from a “magic bullet,” citing an unsourced “1 in 100 to 1 in 10,000” figure without identifying a study, dataset, or denominator.

How can five documented non-exit cases involving these similar cartridges exist if this supposedly occurs only once in every 100 to 10,000 cases?

Were all five bullets “magic bullets”?

Four more examples below.
